neet_che_u17_t02_1.working: Phenol (pKa about 10) is a weaker acid than carbonic acid (pKa about 6.4). So it cannot decompose NaHCO3. It does react with Na metal, NaOH and KOH.

neet_che_u17_t02_2.working: pKa values: p-nitrophenol 7.15, o-nitrophenol 7.2 (lowered by intramolecular H-bonding), m-nitrophenol 8.4 (-I effect only), phenol 10. Decreasing acidity is p > o > m > phenol.

neet_che_u17_t02_3.working: The CH3 group in p-cresol is electron-donating (+I and hyperconjugation), which destabilises the phenoxide ion. So p-cresol is less acidic than phenol, while the nitrophenols are more acidic.

neet_che_u17_t02_4.working: A is true: phenol (pKa about 10) is more acidic than ethanol (pKa about 16). R is false and reversed: phenol's resonance involves charge separation, whereas phenoxide delocalises its negative charge with no charge separation, so delocalisation is more effective in phenoxide.

neet_che_u17_t02_5.working: Statement I is wrong: o-nitrophenol is slightly less acidic than p-nitrophenol because intramolecular H-bonding holds the O-H proton. Statement II is wrong: a meta nitro group acts only through -I, so the para isomer (-R and -I) is more acidic.
